output.title: Synthetic test data: use it to test a real workflow decision
output.body:
Synthetic test data is useful only when it helps you decide faster, not when it becomes a project of its own. For a small business, the bounded question is simple: are you building synthetic data because you need privacy or scale, or because no one has actually tried the workflow with real records yet?

If the pilot is a repeatable task like invoice handling or customer inquiry triage, start smaller. Use a limited real-data subset, clear rules, and a human approval step where money or another high-risk decision is involved. That keeps the discussion on the workflow instead of on the theatre of perfect fake data.

Bareni’s own accounts-payable demo is a good boundary marker. It uses entirely synthetic data to show the mechanics: text-based extraction, arithmetic checks, duplicate blocking, and audit records. But the limits matter too: the default route uses pre-extracted files, and PDF/scan ingestion and OCR are not implemented. So the demo is useful for showing control logic, not for pretending it is ready for every real invoice pile.

The practical next step is simple: pick one workflow, one approval rule, and one small batch of real records. Then ask whether synthetic data is solving a real testing problem, or just postponing the moment you learn what the workflow actually needs. If that question is still fuzzy, the spreadsheet may be doing its usual quiet work.
